commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Kess ({1}{U}{B}{R}, flying) grants one instant/sorcery cast from the graveyard during each of her controller's own turns; exile replacement applies to spells cast via this permission. Her signature Consultation/Tainted Pact into Thassa's Oracle, Intuition/Gifts Reanimate piles, Displacer Kitten new-object reset and Breach/LED/Brain Freeze/Grinding Station engines remain intact. Rev1 adds Mana Drain on-own-turn interaction, unconditional recastable Grim Tutor, commander-enabled Jeska's Will resource generation, recastable Cyclonic Rift and conditional multiplayer Exotic Orchard color access; all five physically replace weaker or role-constrained incumbents and preserve Kess's distinct graveyard-replay ceiling.
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Bracket 5 — fringe cEDH. Current authoritative Rev1 has 23 Game Changers (21 baseline plus Cyclonic Rift and Jeska's Will); 27 lands; 100 distinct cards and no project exception. Tournament selection observations are not controlled outcome evidence. Kess's commander-first Consultation/Intuition/Gifts and own-turn spell replay differentiate her despite shared cEDH mana/counter cores.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: The exact five-swap Rev1 reinforces Kess-specific casting: tutors, rituals and removal are live again from her own graveyard on her own turn. Mana Drain only counters a spell when there is a legal spell on the stack during Kess's turn; Jeska's Will is not guaranteed positive mana against a small hand; Exotic Orchard is conditional fixing. The baseline's Personal Tutor, Counsel and Ledger Shredder were owner additions/keeps; Jeska's Will was previously cut: these are explicitly disclosed reversals now separately approved by Cory on 2026-10-24, not prior permissions silently presumed. All Oracle/Consult, Intuition/Gifts, Displacer Kitten, Entomb, Brain Freeze/Breach, and relevant resilience pieces remain.

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps: All 99 baseline slots were challenged by category: 27 lands, fast mana/rocks, 10 creatures, 30 instants, 13 sorceries, 15 artifacts, 4 enchantments (excluding commander; overlap roles are possible); attention to color thresholds, tutor congestion, interaction and graveyard recast. The final Rev1 has 27 lands, 9 creatures, 31 instants, 13 sorceries, 15 artifacts, 4 enchantments; Kess as commander. The previously accepted 41-card Oct14 rebuild remains historical, while five exact contemporary improvements are selected without replacing the cEDH identity engine.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: Baseline and Rev1 both have 27 lands. Fiery Islet's guaranteed U/R and late card-sacrifice option are exchanged for Exotic Orchard's potential U/B/R, conditional on opponents' land production. There is no unconditional added black source. Blue Force pitch cards 26 to 25; 72 library nonland average MV 1.84722 to 1.90278, and 21 to 23 Game Changers. Kess demands an exact UBR plus generic and Mana Drain an exact UU; do not treat colorless acceleration as UBR fixing.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Core Force of Will, Force of Negation, Fierce Guardianship, Flusterstorm, Pact, Swan Song, Mental Misstep, Mindbreak Trap, Pyroblast, Red Elemental Blast, Deflecting Swat and An Offer remain; Mana Drain adds unconditional hard countering. Deadly Rollick, Toxic Deluge, Chain of Vapor, Otawara survive. Cyclonic Rift over Maw loses a 1-mana emergency bounce and gains no-gift generic nonland reach and conditional expensive board reset. Vulnerable to graveyard hate, Drannith/Rule of Law effects, colored mana and own-turn limitation.

whole_deck_audit.current_baseline_strength: An approved Bracket 5 fringe cEDH Kess list (2026-10-14) after an owner 41-quantity rebuild. M6 Pass C (owner-equivalent substitute, NOT independent) returned NEEDS TESTING and retained the list, with two requested comparisons: +Jeska's Will -Ledger Shredder and +Frantic Search -Personal Tutor. whole_deck_audit.candidate_pool_scope: 25 prior GrokBot material judgments and 14 complete bounded stage-I alternatives are retained as evidence; this independent revisit added post-floor six- and seven-swap exact full-100 counterfactuals, a direct candidate-specific Kess five-swap review and explicit October 24 EDHREC Top/inclusion and off-ranking opportunities. Five is a floor, not a search limit.
whole_deck_audit.off_ranked_search_conclusion: Beyond ranking/popularity, evaluated spell replay support (Muddle the Mixture, Frantic Search), conditional lands (Gemstone Mine, Undercity Sewers, Exotic Orchard), early interaction alternatives (Spell Pierce, Dispel), and owner-disallowed slow generic engines (The One Ring, Opposition Agent, Dauthi Voidwalker). Higher-count alternatives lose the free storm counter and commander ramp; they are staged, not merely dismissed.

material_candidates.role: {U}{U} instant: counter target spell; at the beginning of your next main phase add {C} equal to its mana value.
material_candidates.incumbent_opportunity_cost: Personal Tutor is an owner addition from the 2026-10-14 rebuild (one of the 41 adds; not in the adversarial second pass and not spine-named). {U} sorcery: search for a sorcery and put it on top of the library. It cannot find the instant win pieces (Demonic Consultation, Tainted Pact, Brain Freeze), puts the card on top rather than in hand (a dead draw step unless paired with a draw), and overlaps Mystical Tutor (instant, any instant or sorcery) inside a 14-card tutor suite. Lowest adoption in the 99: EDHREC cEDH 26/387 (6.7%); absent from the stats.cedh.events 61-card staple list; no EDHTop16 aggregate row. Alternative cut (staged, owner-respecting): Deadly Rollick, a free exile spell retained from the original list (not an owner addition; EDHREC cEDH 106/387).
material_candidates.commander_synergy: Kess recasts it from the graveyard on her own turn (paid {U}{U}, normal timing): cast in the precombat main phase or combat, its mana arrives in the postcombat main phase of the same turn (Mana Drain ruling 2020-11-10), so a protected combo turn refunds mana. From hand it is a hard counter at instant speed on any turn. It is a blue card for Force of Will / Force of Negation pitch, keeping the blue count at 26.
material_candidates.adversarial_downside: UU is the strictest blue cost among the counters (bounded P(UU available) turn 2-6 0.50/0.67/0.74/0.80/0.84). Kess gives no permission on opponents' turns, so the graveyard recast only works against spells cast during your turn. Delirium proxy drops by at most about 1.5 points (Personal Tutor is a sorcery; Mana Drain an instant). Spellbook 6 -> 6. Owner-direction flag: the cut overrides an owner addition; fallback +Mana Drain -Deadly Rollick staged.
material_candidates.reason: SELECT_ADD over Oct14 owner-added Personal Tutor after independent challenge: a hard counter that can protect own-turn Kess Consultation and may generate next-main-phase colorless mana only on a legal countered spell. UU, tutor loss and no opponent-turn Kess recast disclosed.

final_changes.coherent_package_tradeoff: Five substantive one-for-one upgrades trade a narrow topdeck tutor for a hard counter, unreliable delirium-only Counsel for unconditional Grim, Shredder connive/blue pitch for commander-enabled Jeska resource compression, one-mana gifted bounce for broadly flexible Rift, and a guaranteed U/R draw-land for conditional U/B/R Orchard. Kess Consultation/Intuition/Gifts and Breach engines all remain; no artificial tempo/ramp cuts are hidden.

low_swap_heightened_audit.alternate_cuts_for_prior_holds: Mana Drain over Deadly Rollick, Grim Tutor over Personal Tutor, Jeska's Will + Frantic Search over Ledger Shredder + Personal Tutor, and counter-heavy Mana Drain + Spell Pierce over Personal Tutor + Fellwar Stone were challenged. Our chosen five retains Rollick/Stone and rejects Frantic's uncertain three-land refund. Owner consent expressly supersedes previous Oct14 Jeska/Counsel/Tutor choices only for this exact Rev1.
low_swap_heightened_audit.strongest_argument_against_baseline: Owner's Oct14 list is a strong 100 but Counsel cannot tutor a card without delirium (no Demon), Personal Tutor only topdecks a sorcery and competes with Mystical Tutor, and Shredder's slow connive may be less decisive than Jeska's mana/impulse recast. Maw cannot produce Rift's multi-permanent late reset, and Islet cannot supply black.
low_swap_heightened_audit.evidence_based_answer: Five meaningful replacements survive this whole-99 / off-ranking / owner-protected challenge, selected as an interacting package after testing 14 prior full-100 counterfactuals and source-valid six-/seven-swap alternatives. All losses (one blue Force pitch, Shredder connive, Tutor to top, Maw one-mana play, Islet card draw and conditional Orchard) explicitly surfaced for owner choice; no measured win-rate increase claimed.

final_candidate.deckwide_reconciliation: Exact 100 physical unique (one Kess commander + 99 library; no basics/companion) sorted commander-first and terminal LF. Five exact additions/cuts against frozen Oct14 baseline 93d27d605bbdf0737ebe32c911fafe3a002b06d7d90f00b7bfc402cb1d3faccb; 27 lands, 25 blue Force pitch cards, 23 Game Changers, avg library nonland mana value 1.90278. Independent Oracle/Commander legality verified 100/100 in October23 live-Scryfall archive and focused CI; earlier one-swap M6 IJ does not automatically transfer.

open_ended_optimization_audit.remaining_99_review: After reaching five, challenged at least eight retained roles: Mindbreak Trap vs Muddle the Mixture; Fellwar Stone vs Spell Pierce; City of Traitors vs Undercity Sewers; Final Fortune vs Frantic Search; Deadly Rollick vs Mana Drain alternate cut; Displacer Kitten vs Notion Thief; Ponder vs Praetor's Grasp; Windfall vs Timetwister. Each loses a relevant Kess early interaction, commander reset, tutoring or fast-mana quality. No sixth was assumed undesirable solely on count.

post_floor_challenges.tradeoff: Muddle offers a costly 1UU transmute to Oracle/Breach and own-turn counter, but losing a conditional free spell-exile trap is a serious turn-zero defense regression versus cEDH storm; UU casting also strains Kess.
Pierce is cheaper reactive protection but stops taxing after turns and loses the two-mana Fellwar source that accelerates and colors the four-mana Kess commander.
Tapped surveil dual land aids graveyard and UB consistency but sacrifices the exceptionally fast two-colorless burst that can accelerate Kess or early Breach infrastructure.

Frantic Search mills/selects for Kess and untaps up to three lands; 27-land configuration often has fewer than three, while Final Fortune grants a second Kess turn and decisive protected combo attempt.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: A sixth recastable UU counter with 1UU transmute can tutor Oracle or Breach and synergize with Kess while reducing need for a purely defensive storm slot.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: It loses Mindbreak Trap, one of the most important free stack-exile defensive answers against storm, and adds a slow 1UU tutoring activation in a three-color deck already rich in faster general tutors.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: A seven-change stack and transmute portfolio creates extra cheap noncreature counterplay and a flexible Oracle/Breach transmute line, while keeping the selected five's tutor/mana/bounce upgrades.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: It simultaneously trades away free Mindbreak Trap and the two-mana Fellwar Stone ramp required for casting a four-mana Grixis commander; this weakens both fast-defense and colored-development axes for marginal late soft permission.

open_ended_optimization_audit.quality_based_stop_reason: The six- and seven-change full-100 variants survive literal legality but fail the Kess commander-first opportunity-cost challenge: free Mindbreak Trap exile and colored early Fellwar ramp matter more than one expensive transmute or soft permission. Other additional challenged incumbent cuts (City, Kitten, Fortune, Ponder, Rollick, Windfall) destroy burst development, an additional Kess permission, a second turn, efficient cantrip setup or graveyard synergy. Thus selecting five is a consequence of judged slot quality and engine retention, not a swap-count stop rule.
